LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To talk about things you can see in different places 
in the world and things you can buy or do in a shop.
MATERIALS
•	 TR#2 Moods Version 1
•	 TR#18 Genie in a Bottle Song
•	 TR#19 Travel with me Song
•	 TR#20 Time to Go Home
•	 Moods A5 flash cards
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 8: Country flash cards (P.4.3)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 4: Country flash cards (P.4.3)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 7: Country Bingo boards + 
Attraction cards (P.4.7) + counters
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 1: A3 Map (P.4.1) + Country 
cutouts + cloth bag
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 9: Number cards (P.E.M.3)
•	 Big Book
•	 Crayons or pencils

•	 Blu-Tack
LESSON PLAN
1.– WARM-UP ROUTINES (10’)
•	 Hello + register + booklets
•	 Moods, TR#2 (optional)
•	 My Pet
2.– STORY (PP.9-17) (9’)
Tell the students the second half of the story using the Big 
Book. Please see the section on storytelling in the Warm-Up 
Routines Index. Before telling the second half of the story, it is 
advisable to ask some recap questions such as: 
•	 “What were Pam and Paul doing in the attic?” 
“They were helping Grandma clean the attic.” 
•	 “What did they find in the attic?” 
“They found a (big brown) suitcase with lots of 
stickers all over it.”

•	 “Which countries did Grandma go to?”  
“Grandma went to America, Australia, India and 
Africa.” 
•	 “What was in Grandma’s suitcase?”  
“In Grandma’s suitcase there was an old-looking 
glass bottle.”
3.– ACTIVITY 5: RIGHT OR WRONG? (8’)
> How to Play
Show the Ss different pages from the Big Book and say a 
sentence about them. The Ss then have to decide if it is right 
or wrong.
> Warm-Up
Start off with some easy statements. Say for example, “Paul 
is a girl. Is that right or wrong?”. The Ss should then reply, “No, 
that’s wrong! Paul is a boy.” Say two or three more statements 
and make them correct you.
> Main Activity
Introduce the activity by saying, “Let’s see how well you 
remember the story.”. Divide the Ss into two teams. Show the 
Ss different pages from the Big Book and say a right or wrong 
statement. For example, “Pam, Paul and Grandpa are cleaning 
the attic. Is that right or wrong?”. The Ss should respond, 
“That’s wrong!” and then correct it by saying “Pam, Paul and 
Grandma are cleaning the attic.” The Ss can decide together as 
a group whether the phrase is true or false, but they must take 
turns to reply. Every time one of the teams answers correctly, 
they get a point.
4.– WORKSHEET: STORY COMPREHENSION (P.5) (9’)
Story Comprehension

MATERIALS
•	 Crayons or pencils

NOTE: if you collected your Ss’ books during the booklet 
activity, have them ask you for it now by saying, “Can I have 
my book please?”; otherwise, ask them to take it out of their 
bag. Explain the activity before giving out the books/asking Ss 
to take them out since they might get distracted.
Before identifying if they are right or wrong, ask the Ss to 
describe the scenes asking, “What is happening here?” to 
which Ss should reply for example, “Pam, Paul, and Grandpa 
are cleaning the attic.” Then ask, “Is that right or is that 
wrong?”. You can show the Ss the Big Book if they have issues 
remembering the story. The Ss then decide, and in this case 
say, “That’s wrong, Grandpa isn’t cleaning the attic, Grandma 
is.” Everybody should then circle the red cross in the box. If the 
image is correct, they say, “That’s right!” and circle the green 
tick in the box.

6.– ACTIVITY 8: TRAVEL WITH ME SONG (TR#19) (2’) 
> How to Play
Get the Ss to stand up in a circle and distribute the flash 
cards of the ten countries mentioned in the song. Introduce the 
activity by saying, “Let’s sing and travel around the world!”. The 
Ss should sing the song and perform the related movements. 
When a country is mentioned, the S holding that flash card 
should step forward and turn around in the circle showing their 
classmates the card before returning to their place.
TRAVEL WITH ME SONG
C’mon, c’mon
Come with me 
(make a “come here” motion with your arm by 
stretching it out and then bringing it towards yourself)
Let’s travel the world and see what we can see 
(hold out arms at your sides like an airplane and then 
hold your hand above your eyes as if protecting them 
from the sun and look around)
We can see kangaroos in Australia
And the Statue of Liberty in America
We can see elephants in Africa
And visit the pyramids in Egypt
(chorus)
We can see polar bears in Canada
And visit the Alhambra in Spain
We can visit the Great Wall in China
And the Eiffel Tower in France
(chorus)
We can visit Big Ben in England
And the Taj Mahal in India
So many places for us to see
So come on, come on, travel with me
7.– ACTIVITY 4: WHERE ARE YOU FROM? (8’)
P.4.3
Italy

> How to Play
Ss must ask and answer questions about where they and their 
classmates are from according to the flash cards they pick up.
> Warm-Up
First, model the activity. Choose a Country flash card (P.4.3) 
and ask the Ss, “Can you guess where I’m from?”. Say for 
example, “Where I’m from, you can see Big Ben, people speak 
English, and it’s always rainy.”. The Ss must guess by asking, 
“Are you from England?” and then, you must respond by saying 
either “Yes, I am,” or “No, I am not.”
> Main Activity
A Ss chooses a Country flash card (P.4.3) and keeps it a secret 
from the rest. The group then asks, “Where are you from?”. 
The S should give clues using the following structures:
•	 Where I’m from people speak…
•	 Where I’m from you can see…
•	 Where I’m from people eat…
•	 Where I’m from you can visit…
Ss must guess their classmate’s country by asking for 
example, “Are you from Australia?” to which the S should 
reply, “Yes, I am,” or “No, I am not.” Make sure that every S 
participates either by taking a country or by asking questions. 
As it can take a long time for all Ss to have a go at this activity 
we recommend that you take a note of any Ss that didn’t get 
a go so they can go first the following day.
> Follow-Up
Ask Ss quick questions about the country they are from. 
Say, “What language do people speak where you are from?”, 
“What can you see there?”, “What do people eat?”, “What can 
you visit?”. Let the group come up with ideas and respond by 
saying: “Where I’m from…”
8.– ACTIVITY 7: COUNTRIES MEMORY LOTTO (9’)
P.4.7
South Africa
China
Argentina
P.4.7
P.4.7

> How to Play
For this game, Ss must match the attractions on the Memory 
cards (P.4.7) with the countries on their Bingo boards (P.4.7).
> Warm-Up
Show the Ss one of the boards. Point to a country and ask, 
“Where did you go? What did you see or visit there?” to which 
Ss should reply for example, “I went to Brazil to visit Christ the 
Redeemer.” Ask a few more Ss about the rest of the countries 
on the board.
> Main Activity
Give each S one Bingo board and place the Memory cards 
face down in the middle of the table. Introduce the activity by 
saying “Let’s talk about the places we travelled to and what 
we saw there!”.
To play, a S turns over a memory card which shows something 
you can see or do in a certain country.
If it is a match the S must say, “I went to South Africa to see 
elephants. It’s a pair. Can I have a counter, please?”
If it is not a match, they must say, “I didn’t go to South Africa 
to see kangaroos; I went to South Africa to see elephants. 
It’s not a pair.”
Adapt the target language (eat, go, see, visit) as needed.
> Follow-Up
When a S finishes their board or time has run out, ask a S 
about their board by saying, “Where did you go and what did 
you do there?” to which the S should reply, “I went to India to 
visit the Taj Mahal, to Canada to see polar bears and to Spain 
to visit the Alhambra.”

10.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (2’) 
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the Ss form a line 
before leaving the class.
BONUS
ACTIVITY 9: NUMBERS (VERSION 1) 
P.E.M.3
55
> Main Activity
The goal of the game is to find as many cards as possible. 
Stick some of the Number Cards (P.E.M.3.) on the wall (out 
of reach of the Ss, so they can’t damage them). Say, “Find 
number...” and have the Ss run and point to the corresponding 
number. When the S points to the correct number, take it off 
the wall and keep it as a point for that S. The S who collects 
the most cards wins.
NOTE: this game can become hectic if everybody is playing 
at the same time. It is advisable to play this game in duels of 
two Ss (S1 vs S2). You call out the number and the two Ss must 
race to point to the card first.

TARGET LANGUAGE
I saw elephants in South Africa.
I saw kangaroos in Australia.
I saw polar bears in Canada.
I saw lemurs in Madagascar.
I visited the Statue of Liberty in the United States of America.
I visited the pyramids in Egypt.
I visited the Great Wall in China.
I visited the Taj Mahal in India.
I visited Big Ben in England.
I visited the Alhambra in Spain.
I visited the Eiffel Tower in France.
I went to the Black Forest in Germany.
I visited the Leaning Tower of Pisa in Italy.
I visited Christ the Redeemer in Brazil.
I visited Mount Fuji in Japan.
I visited Patagonia in Argentina.
> Main Activity
Use Blu-Tack to stick the Map (P.4.1) up on the whiteboard. 
Then take the Country cutouts and put them in a cloth bag. 
The Ss take it in turns to take a country from the bag. Ask the 
S, “Where did you go?” and have them respond by saying, “I 
went to Brazil.” Then ask, “What did you visit in Brazil?”, 
and have the S respond according to what is pictured on the 
cutout, “I visited Christ the Redeemer in Brazil.”. Then the S 
places the country on the map in the correct space. Do as many 
countries as time allows.
NOTE: your Ss are likely to need support the first couple 
times you do this activity. Do not hesitate to help them come 
up with the name of the places. Accept any other ideas as long 
as they are correct, and the S has used the target structure.
